07-evaluation.tex.fileSummary: Chapter 7 (Evaluation) draws three dominant themes of supervisor concern. Smaller but real: RQ wording drift from Chapter 1, the missing agent-feedback/PoC cross-links to the RQ map, and several concluding paragraphs that Kritikos wants added.

02-related-work.tex.fileSummary: Kritikos's 53 comments on the Related Work chapter cluster around three dominant themes. First, taxonomy and terminology rigor: he insists linting is not testing (it is static analysis / verification), that "contract testing" must be split into consumer-driven vs provider-driven sub-types (with Dredd reclassified as provider-driven), and that the chapter's paradigm should be called "Specification-Driven" to match the SDT name rather than "Documentation-driven." Second, a sustained challenge to the Table 2.1 "single-artifact" criterion (echoing headline points 3 and his repeated inline pushback at idx 86-89, 96): he argues every testing tool already consumes a single artifact (the OpenAPI spec), so the criterion as worded is wrong and either its definition or the per-tool evaluations must change. Third, a structural proposal to move the OpenAPI Ecosystem section to the front (as Section 2.1) and merge/clarify the overlapping Dredd section, plus a recurring demand to (a) correlate research gaps with the DriveBy tool and Chapter 4 (headline #4), (b) clarify whether validation/reconciliation targets the spec, the source code, or both, and (c) reference the agent-driven reconciliation evaluation in several places (headline #1).
